quotas.description: Exactly one approved allocation for each logical runtime, state, scratch and logs bucket. Array order has no authority; duplicate bucket names are invalid even when native allocations differ.

CapacitySnapshot.description: Accounting by one receiving authority for the exact accepted resource generation and verified adapter bindings. Each quota must join the observed pool identity exactly; canonical capacity domains and allocation handles cannot be counted twice. qualified/enforced are observations whose native evidence the owner must verify, never assertions a source may grant. Admission must independently compare the snapshot to current accepted bindings and freshness before reserving capacity.

CapacityRequest.description: Bounded growth under independently loaded, accepted resource authority. bindings_digest pins the canonical owner, account, resource_generation, control_pool, pools sorted by pool and quotas sorted by bucket. Each pool entry contains pool/storage/reserve_bytes/reserve_inodes; each quota contains bucket/pool/storage/root/max_bytes/max_inodes/headroom_bytes/headroom_inodes. The receiving owner derives the expected digest from independently approved resource bindings and policy, never from an untrusted accounting snapshot or caller request. Changing usage counters, reservations and observation time are excluded. A changed owner epoch, adapter instance, scope, incarnation, capacity domain or approved limit requires fresh admission.

CapacityReservation.description: Owner-held capacity claims retain the exact verified allocation and pool identities, including native incarnations. Reconciliation after restore or re-enrollment cannot transfer a live claim to a replacement binding by name. Timeout or uncertain writer cessation does not release claims.

coverage_complete.description: True only after an exact native traversal has exhausted its stable scoped inventory and all referenced objects and protected roots; page availability, a fixed count, timeout or partial scan cannot establish completeness. False must block destructive cleanup.

max_objects.description: Owner-chosen bound on one deletion dispatch batch. The reviewed CleanupPlan retains the complete candidate extent; this bound does not truncate the plan, inventory or store. All batches share the verified inventory and protection index. Native limits may refuse/delay a batch but cannot silently omit objects or restart unchanged full scans for each batch.

CleanupInventory.description: Native inventory bound to the current accepted owner policy and exact retention inventory. protected_roots and protected_by may add protection but cannot replace or subtract owner-derived retention roots. A missing retained native handle prevents cleanup. minimum_age_seconds may impose a stricter age than the accepted unused-candidate grace, never a weaker one. The receiving owner establishes the complete object, incoming-reference and protected-closure indexes once under exclusion. Any external native identity, edge, use, protection or ownership change invalidates the indexed generation; confirmed own deletions may advance it with authenticated exact outcomes. The complete operation includes every inventory page, reviewed candidate, dispatch batch, retry and affected external update. Its work must be linear in complete input bytes/edges plus attempted candidates and genuinely changed affected extent; copying or rescanning unchanged state is work, not new input. A native implementation that cannot preserve that bound and exact protection must stop rather than discard protection, truncate extent or claim qualification.

max_objects.description: Maximum candidates in one dispatch batch, preserving the complete reviewed candidates across all batches. A lower current owner limit may make batches smaller without widening permission.

retention_inventory_digest.description: Digest of the complete retention observation reviewed when this plan was prepared. It preserves provenance; a later timestamp-only refresh need not reproduce it.

retention_custody_digest.description: Digest of the complete RetentionInventory canonical JSON with only its top-level observed_at omitted. Every other field remains pinned, including policy and owner identity, protection generation, completeness, release ordering timestamps, runtime references, holds, archive validity/evidence and cold-demotion receipts.

CleanupPlan.description: Exact complete cleanup proposal bound to accepted policy, stable retention custody and protection generation. max_objects limits dispatch batches, never the reviewed candidate extent. The candidate extent is the eligible, currently unreferenced frontier in this reviewed inventory. Confirmed removal never adds newly unreferenced dependencies to that intent. Completion accounts for every listed candidate; it does not claim whole-store reclamation to a fixed point. Any broader reclamation implementation must measure its aggregate graph visits and work across all resulting plans and cannot use repeated review to hide nonlinear rescanning. inventory_digest and retention_inventory_digest retain the original complete observations for provenance; retention_custody_digest excludes only the top-level retention observed_at. protection_digest binds policy_digest, retention_custody_digest, protection_generation and the complete protected closure. The owner verifies the complete graph once, then before every deletion or retry checks its independently current owner/account/store identity, accepted policy digest, exact retention custody, protection generation, indexed native generation, observation freshness, current durability/exclusive-control status and exact candidate kind/native identity. This constant-size custody check is valid only while actual owner-held exclusion prevents external policy, hold, recovery-reference and native graph changes. The owner retains exclusion through the authenticated native outcome; only confirmed own removal advances indexed generation. Unknown outcomes or any lost exclusion invalidate the traversal and require reconciliation, never a blind retry. Cold archive validity and plan expiry remain enforced even when generations do not change. A reviewed plan cannot override policy or release holds. The reference model supplies neither locks nor authentication: its non-serializable exclusion and current custody inputs represent independently held native owner facts, not requester assertions. Complete-operation growth includes all pages, batches, retries and affected external invalidations; repeated full-state copies or rescans cannot be hidden as independent batches or fresh input. Native continuation after invalidation must maintain an exact index with a linear work proof; the reference traversal stops and makes no claim to implement that continuation.

CleanupReceipt.description: Complete accounting of an exact reviewed cleanup selection. owner, operation_id, plan_digest and account equal the enclosing Operation and its reviewed account; admission independently verifies the application-to-account mapping. items contains every selected candidate exactly once and no others, including blocked or unresolved candidates. verified-complete requires every outcome removed or already-absent; skipped and failed outcomes remain incomplete. Any unknown outcome requires effect-unknown and the enclosing Operation has unknown effect certainty. A succeeded Operation requires verified-complete and known effects. Partial/blocked receipts preserve all selected items rather than dropping unfinished work. Byte totals are observations, not authorization or proof of attributable reclaimed space.

storage.description: Exactly one entry for each logical storage bucket: runtime, state, scratch and logs. Order is immaterial; a duplicate bucket cannot stand in for missing coverage, even when its measurements or allocation identity differ.

complete.description: True only after every retained release and runtime/protection reference in this owner scope has been exhaustively traversed; no fixed number of entries establishes completeness. False blocks reclamation.

verified_at.description: Verified release-closure instant used for hot-predecessor ordering. Compare the parsed UTC instant, not the timestamp text; release_digest is the deterministic descending tie-break only for equal instants.

RetentionInventory.description: Current owner-verified release and custody closure under the exact AcceptedRetentionPolicy digest. protection_generation changes whenever retained references, holds or recovery obligations change. This inventory supplies evidence, never replacement retention policy. Its sole accepted release must match the accepted policy release.

max_observation_age_seconds.description: Maximum permitted age of both complete retention and native cleanup observations, independently approved by the receiving owner. Planning and every deletion revalidation use this same current setting. A requester, adapter or plan cannot relax it; a change creates a new accepted policy generation.

AcceptedRetentionPolicy.description: Current retention policy read from the receiving owner's accepted state. policy is the exact retention object from the accepted application source, and release_digest identifies that accepted release. max_observation_age_seconds is the receiving owner's independently approved observation-freshness setting. The owner changes generation whenever any accepted policy setting changes. Supplied fields and schema validation do not authorize acceptance or a policy change; callers must obtain this record independently from current owner state, not from the cleanup requester or adapter.

ColdDemotionReceipt.description: Owner-authenticated authorization to demote the named local recovery closure under the exact accepted policy, archive evidence and protection generation. It never overrides keep-local or any hold. Native owners authenticate its provenance before supplying it to the reference decision model; matching digest fields alone do not authenticate a receipt.
